task_instance: Run the prd-start workflow to begin implementation on PRD 12 (User Data Export) in a small sample git repo: detect the forge, validate PRD readiness, assign the tracking issue to the current user, create the feature branch, and produce the handoff to prd-next.
blocker_detail: The skill's Step 3 is explicitly MANDATORY and is also listed in its Success Criteria: it must assign the forge issue to the current user (e.g. 'gh issue edit <id> --add-assignee @me') to signal work-in-progress and prevent duplicate pickup. This inherently requires an authenticated forge account and an external-service write. The sandbox has the gh CLI but it is not authenticated (the provided token is invalid), there is no real remote/repo/issue, and the safety rules forbid using credentials, account-bound services, and writes to external services. Per the stop rule I did not work around it. The remaining, non-service parts of the workflow were completed and verified locally: forge detection (no origin remote), PRD discovery and selection, readiness validation against the PRD, feature-branch creation, and the prd-next handoff message.
evidence: Created sample git repo at sample-repo/ with prds/12-user-export.md (functional reqs, measurable success criteria, dependencies, risks, integration points, approach, milestones), committed on main. Ran: git remote get-url origin -> 'No such remote origin' (forge detect step, no remote). git branch --show-current -> main; git checkout -b feature/prd-12-user-export -> branch switched; git branch shows feature/prd-12-user-export and main (branch setup verified). Readiness check and handoff written to readiness-and-handoff.md (all 6 checklist items satisfiable, scope check single valuable outcome). Issue-assignment step: gh auth status reports the GH_TOKEN is invalid (not logged in); no issue-edit write was attempted because it needs an authenticated forge account and is a forbidden external write. glab and tea CLIs are absent. Files: sample-repo/ (git repo, branch feature/prd-12-user-export), readiness-and-handoff.md.
